title: First date paid with a gift card
author: Storytime
hook: My first date insisted on paying with a gift card. Then the manager came to our table.
story: So I matched with this guy, Kyle, and he picked the restaurant. A fancy Italian place downtown. He was charming. He ordered for both of us, which I thought was a little much, but okay. He kept saying, don't worry, tonight is on me. When the bill came, he pulled out a gift card and said, I've been saving this for someone special. The waiter took it. Five minutes later, she came back. Not the waiter. The manager. She looked at the card, then at Kyle, then at me. And she said, sir, this card was purchased by our staff for my birthday last year. I gave it to my boyfriend to hold. In March. Kyle went pale. Because the manager wasn't just the manager. She was his girlfriend. Of two years. They live together. He'd been using her birthday gift card to take other women to her restaurant, on her nights off. Except tonight, someone called in sick. She calmly took the card, cut it in half, and put the pieces on his plate. Then she turned to me and said, your dinner is on the house. And then she slid me a napkin with her number on it, and said, call me, we need to talk. So I did. Part two?
caption: he picked the wrong restaurant 💀 #storytime
sound: a playful, suspenseful jazz piano at very low volume
why: Dating story time is one of the most watched storytime genres, the gift card he was saving for someone special pays off as the reveal, and the manager's number is a natural part two.

title: Uninvited brother was the DJ
author: Storytime
hook: I didn't invite my brother to my wedding. He showed up anyway. As the DJ.
story: Two years ago, my little brother Danny borrowed eight thousand dollars from my wedding fund. He swore he'd pay it back in six months. He never did. He stopped answering my calls. So when the invitations went out, Danny didn't get one. My parents were furious, but I didn't budge. A month before the wedding, our DJ canceled. The venue said not to worry, they had a backup. Some guy called DJ Dee. Weird name, but the reviews were great. On the day, my wife and I walk into the reception, the music starts, and I look up at the DJ booth. It's Danny. In a suit. Headphones on. Grinning like an idiot. I almost walked over and kicked him out. But my wife grabbed my arm and said, wait. And honestly, he was incredible. Everyone danced all night. Even my grandma. At the end, he played our song, the one from our first date, which only family would know. Then he walked up to me and handed me an envelope. Inside was eight thousand dollars in cash. He said he'd been DJing weddings every weekend for two years to pay me back. Including mine. For free. So, do I forgive him?
caption: DJ Dee was my brother the whole time 🎧 #storytime
sound: an emotional, uplifting piano that builds slowly at very low volume
why: Uninvited family at a wedding is a hot drama theme, the strange DJ name is a planted clue, and the redemption twist with the money makes people share it and argue about forgiveness.

title: I trained my replacement
author: Storytime
hook: My boss asked me to train the new hire. On her last day of training, she showed me her offer letter.
story: I've worked at the same marketing agency for five years. Last month, my boss, Brian, asked me to train a new hire, Nina. He said she'd be my assistant, to lighten my workload. I was thrilled. Finally, help. For three weeks I taught her everything. My clients. My passwords. My processes. Nina was smart, and honestly, really kind. On her last day of training, we got coffee, and she looked uncomfortable. Then she slid her phone across the table. It was her offer letter. Her job title was my job title. And her salary was fifteen thousand dollars higher than mine. Brian wasn't hiring me an assistant. He was hiring my replacement, and making me train her for free. Nina said she couldn't take a job built like that. Then she asked me something I didn't expect. She said, how many of your clients would follow you if you left? I counted. Eleven. Out of fourteen. That was six weeks ago. Yesterday, Nina and I signed the lease for our own agency. And this morning, Brian emailed me asking why his biggest client just canceled their contract. Should I answer him?
caption: I trained her. then she trained ME 🤝 #storytime
sound: a confident, rising beat at very low volume
why: Being forced to train your own replacement is a common fear that makes people stop scrolling, the kind new hire flips from threat to ally, and the final question invites petty answers in the comments.
